subject.title: [Bug]: browser navigation-guard explicit hostname allowlist broken by SSRF loopback tightening (#100835)

question: Should browser navigation exact-host allowlist entries continue to allow non-localhost hostnames that resolve to loopback after the trusted-host SSRF hardening, or should that old test contract be retired?
rationale: Both outcomes are plausible: preserving the test restores an operator-declared browser exception, while retiring it keeps the newly accepted SSRF hardening against non-localhost loopback rebinding.

options.title: Retire the old loopback-alias contract
options.body: Keep the hardened trusted-host loopback behavior and update the browser navigation test/docs to require explicit localhost, loopback literals, or reviewed private-network opt-in.

options.title: Approve a scoped browser exception
options.body: Change the browser navigation guard or SSRF policy plumbing so exact browser allowlist entries can intentionally override loopback-resolution blocking without weakening metadata or link-local checks.

options.title: Defer to broader SSRF design
options.body: Keep this issue open as a design item until browser SSRF allowlist semantics are decided alongside related private-network and CDP-control policy work.

recommendation.title: Retire the old loopback-alias contract
recommendation.body: Keep the hardened trusted-host loopback behavior and update the browser navigation test/docs to require explicit localhost, loopback literals, or reviewed private-network opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the related browser/CDP SSRF work and has already handled maintainer proof and merge decisions on the adjacent fixes.
